content.user_title: Run Fluid Dynamics Simulations with FluidSim
content.value_statement: Configuring reproducible CFD experiments across solvers, grids, and HPC environments is complex. This skill guides FluidSim setup, parameter selection, execution, and output analysis.
actual_capabilities: Selects FluidSim solvers for 2D or 3D Navier-Stokes, shallow-water, and stratified-flow problems.
Builds Python parameter configurations for domains, resolution, viscosity, time stepping, initialization, forcing, and output intervals.
Provides workflows for running, restarting, and parallelizing simulations with MPI.
Explains analysis of physical fields, spatial means, spectra, and HDF5 simulation outputs.
Supports parametric study planning and cluster job-script generation.
Suggests FFT backend settings and memory or performance adjustments.
limitations: Requires the FluidSim Python package and compatible FFT dependencies.
Does not replace validation against analytical solutions, experiments, or published benchmarks.
Large 3D simulations require substantial memory, storage, and MPI-capable computing resources.
Examples assume periodic domains and may not fit boundary-driven or complex-geometry flows.

use_cases.title: Plan a turbulence experiment
use_cases.description: Choose a solver, configure resolution and viscosity, define outputs, and prepare a reproducible simulation workflow.

use_cases.title: Prepare an MPI parameter study
use_cases.description: Organize resolution and viscosity sweeps, estimate resources, and structure cluster jobs with separate outputs.

use_cases.title: Learn pseudospectral CFD
use_cases.description: Build a small simulation, inspect vorticity and spectra, and compare results with a known benchmark.

prompt_templates.title: Start a 2D simulation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal FluidSim 2D Navier-Stokes example at 128 by 128 resolution. Explain each parameter and include basic vorticity plotting.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a small local simulation.

prompt_templates.title: Select a solver
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare FluidSim solvers for [physical problem]. Recommend one solver, required parameters, initial conditions, and validation outputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: A user needs to map a physical problem to a supported solver.

prompt_templates.title: Restart and analyze a run
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a restart workflow for [simulation directory]. Include safe parameter changes, spectrum analysis, spatial means, and reproducibility checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A researcher needs to continue and evaluate an existing simulation.

prompt_templates.title: Design an MPI parameter study
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MPI parametric study over [resolutions] and [viscosities]. Estimate resource needs, organize outputs, generate cluster scripts, and define convergence checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a controlled high-performance computing campaign.

output_examples.input: Set up a small 2D turbulence simulation for local testing.
output: Resolution: 128 by 128 with a periodic square domain.
Use noise initialization, adaptive time stepping, conservative viscosity, and vorticity plus spectra outputs.

output_examples.input: Choose a solver for a stratified ocean-flow experiment.
output: Use a stratified Navier-Stokes solver matching the required dimensionality.
Define stratification strength, viscosity, domain size, resolution, and a physically justified initial state.
Track buoyancy, velocity fields, spatial means, and spectra for validation.

output_examples.input: Plan a 512 cubed MPI study across three viscosities.
output: Use the 3D Navier-Stokes solver and estimate memory before launch.
Create separate output directories and job records for every viscosity.
Start with a smaller convergence run before allocating the full MPI workload.

best_practices: Start at low resolution, validate outputs, then increase grid size and MPI resources.
Record physical, numerical, output, software, and hardware settings for every run.
Compare conserved quantities, convergence behavior, and benchmark results before interpreting physical conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not launch high-resolution 3D runs before estimating memory, storage, and wall time.
Do not change solver parameters during restart without checking compatibility with saved state.
Do not infer physical accuracy from stable execution alone.

faq.question: What equations does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers 2D and 3D Navier-Stokes, shallow-water, and stratified-flow solvers documented by FluidSim.

faq.question: Does it install FluidSim automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but users must approve package and system dependency changes.

faq.question: Can it run simulations without MPI?
faq.answer: Yes. Small simulations can run locally, while large three-dimensional workloads usually benefit from MPI.

faq.question: Which output formats are covered?
faq.answer: It covers FluidSim physical fields, spatial means, spectra, and HDF5 outputs for external visualization.

faq.question: Can it validate scientific accuracy?
faq.answer: It suggests convergence and benchmark checks, but domain experts must assess model assumptions and physical accuracy.

faq.question: Does FluidSim require API credentials?
faq.answer: No API credentials are described. Local package, FFT, storage, and optional cluster requirements still apply.
